messages.author: d671b738709ad83e
messages.subject: rstan: dropping chains
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if there was a method already existing to drop unwanted chains? I couldn't find any so I tried to implement this myself but I'm getting a few errors of 'the model object is not created or not valid.' Probably to do with stuff from the .MISC slot. Thanks!



stan_drop_chains <- function(object, chain_ids) {
    if (!is(object, "stanfit"))
        stop("object must be a fitted rstan object")
    
    if (missing(chain_ids))
        stop("please select chain numbers to drop for argument 'chain_ids'")
    
    ids <- unlist(lapply(object@stan_args, function(l) l$chain_id))
    
    drop <- ids %in% chain_ids
    
    if (!any(drop))
        stop("chain_ids not found in stanfit object")
    
    for (chain in seq_along(drop)) {
        if (drop[chain]) {
            object@sim$samples[ids[chain]] <- NULL
            object@inits[ids[chain]] <- NULL
            object@sim$permutation[ids[chain]] <- NULL
            object@stan_args[ids[chain]] <- NULL
        }
    }
    
    object@sim$chains <- length(which(!drop))
    object@sim$n_save <- object@sim$n_save[!drop]
    object@sim$warmup2 <- object@sim$warmup2[!drop]
    
    for (chain in seq_len(object@sim$chains)) {
        object@stan_args[[chain]]$chain_id <- chain
    }
    
    new_obj <- new(
        "stanfit",
        model_name = object@model_name,
        model_pars = object@model_pars,
        par_dims = object@par_dims,
        mode = 0L,
        sim = object@sim,
        inits = object@inits,
        stan_args = object@stan_args,
        stanmodel = object@stanmodel,
        date = date(),
        .MISC = new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    )
    
    return(new_obj)
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: dropping chains
parts:
Please do not drop chains.  Misbehaving chains are serious indicators 
that the “good” chains are also biased.  The only valid reason to drop
a chain would be if you have too many samples for R to handle well, 
but in that case you can just rerun with fewer iterations.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: dropping chains
parts:
Do you want to drop entire chains or take a subset of posterior draws? It's not easy to drop a chain from a stanfit object really, but you can easily take a sample from the array of posterior draws as you would with any array in R, or drop a chain from the array. The resulting array can still be used with shinystan (albeit with some limitations) although not with the plotting functions in RStan. However that functionality is coming soon when we standardize the plotting functionality across all of our R packages using a new and more flexible and dependency free (except for ggplot really) package. That should be ready at some point this summer.

Jonah

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: dropping chains
parts:
What are you trying to accomplish? As Michael said,
if you want to drop chains that didn't converge, that
will potentially lead to biased estimates.

If you just want to subsample because there's too much
data, you want to thin existing chains rather than cut
out whole chains. That way, the convergence diagnostics
and effective sample size estimates are reasonable. If you
just permute, you lose all of this.

- Bob
